title: Knuckle Rush - Demo available
author: Darkonxy
selftext:
Hey guys!

I've just released a new gameplay video featuring several improvements based on feedback from the community!

The demo is also available here:  
[https://knucklerush.itch.io/knuckle-rush](https://knucklerush.itch.io/knuckle-rush)

I'd love to hear what you think! Any constructive feedback is more than welcome and will help me keep improving the game.

Thanks for your support!

comments.author: aigamedev-mod
comments.body:
Hey u/Darkonxy, this falls under Rule 4. Commercial posts are okay here, but you need to talk about how it was developed using AI, so the community has something to discuss. This post doesn't have enough on that yet.

To keep it up, edit your post or reply to this comment within an hour with some details on your dev process, like:

- which AI tools you used, and what for
- how they fit into your workflow
- problems you hit and how you dealt with them

"Made with AI", a list of tools or a ChatGPT bullet list won't cut it. If nothing's added by then, this post may be removed.

If you think we got this wrong, [message the mods](https://www.reddit.com/message/compose?to=/r/aigamedev).

comments.author: ishmaellius
comments.body:
This is pretty cool! 

I recently made an arcade cabinet and started putting the games I've made on it.  Reason I bring it up, I feel like your game fits exactly into this awkward category of "really cool on a cabinet - totally would play if I saw it in the real world but otherwise is hard to place elsewhere".

Couple things - overall very good level of uniform polish across the characters, the sprites, the environment, the interactables.  I think this uniformity and cohesion is one of the first places that "AI" starts to reveal itself and lose people.  Your game is really well done on that department.  One area I noticed it's missing though - the combo highlight - it's still just flat single lines which stands out against everything else. 

What's your plan for the game? Release to itch? Anywhere else? Like I said, I've got a few of these "arcade style" games now and I'm curious how you're thinking about it.  There's always more levels, more characters, 2P co op, etc which I assume you probably already have planned or even implemented, but I'm just curious what your ultimate goal is for it?
